podcast.body: Originally included on the album "(What's the Story) Morning Glory?", this song was later removed from all subsequent editions, increasing the value of the original album. The removal and subsequent changes to its credits were a result of a lawsuit due to its similarity to Stevie Wonder's 1966 hit "Uptight Everything's All Right." Following the court case, post-Morning Glory versions of "Step Out" list Noel Gallagher, Stevie Wonder, Sylvia Moe, and Henry Cosby as writers, with Wonder, Moe, and Cosby each receiving at least a quarter of the proceeds. "Oasis was taken to court. And if you look at any post Morning Glory version of Step Out, like an Alive album or something, you'll see that it is listed as being written by No of Yalger and three other people."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Originally on the *What's the Story (Morning Glory)?* album, this song sounded too much like Stevie Wonder's 1966 hit "Uptight (Everything's All Right)." Stevie Wonder successfully pursued legal action, and "all subsequent editions of the album had that song removed." Noel Gallagher's songwriting credit and royalties were reduced, with three other people also credited, leading to Noel receiving "just 25%" of royalties. "This was also taken by Stevie Wonder over a song called Step Out from What's the Story Morning Glory album which sounded way too much life as 1966 hit Uptight Everything's All Right."

podcast.body: Included on the "(What's the Story) Morning Glory" album. This song was found to be too similar to Stevie Wonder's 1966 hit "Uptight (Everything's All Right)." Stevie Wonder won his complaint, resulting in the song's removal from all subsequent editions of the album. Consequently, Noel Gallagher's royalty share for the song was reduced from 100% to 25%, shared with three other credited individuals. "This was also taken, by Stevie Wonder, over a song called Step Out from What's the Story Morning Glory album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
